Learned counsel also contended that prior to registration of the claim petition before the Tribunal, the claimants wrongly instituted a petition before the permanent Lok Adalat in MVC No.76/2009 and the order passed by the permanent Lok Adalat was challenged by the respondent herein in W.P.No.60510/2011 on the ground that permanent Lok Adalat had no jurisdiction to decide the Motor Vehicles Claim cases and the appellants had also filed W.P.No.68571/2011 seeking enhancement of compensation.

 claimants are not entitled for any enhancement?
Issue No.2.

In his evidence, he has reiterated the contention taken up in the written statement.
On the other hand, the claimant No.1 was examined as PW-1 and reiterated her contention as taken in the petition.

As per the contents of Ex-P2 FIR, Ex-P3 complaint,
Ex-P4 spot panchanama and Ex-P6 charge sheet, it appears that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KA-22-F-1541.

9. Sofar as quantum is concerned, the accident is of the year 2009 and the notional income is to be taken at Rs.5,000/- but the Tribunal has considered Rs.4,000/- which is not reasonable one.

At the time of accident, the deceased was aged 44 years and he was working as a Manager and the appropriate multiplier applicable is '14' and for his age group,
25% is to be considered towards his future prospects.
If Rs.5,000/- is multiplied by 12, it would be Rs.60,000/-.
If Rs.15,000/- is added to Rs.60,000/-, it would be Rs.75,000/-.
As per the Sarla Verma's case, if the dependants are more than 6, 1/5th has to be taken in the total income towards living and personal expenses.

In MFA No.103487/2018, petitioner Nos.1 and 4 are  -9-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7938  MFA No. 103487 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 102302 of 2017 the first and second wife and petitioner Nos.2, 3 and 5 to 7 are children and they are dependants of the deceased.

Therefore,
1/5th share has to be deducted in Rs.75,000/-, 1/5th of Rs.75,000/- would be Rs.15,000/-.
If Rs.15,000/- is deducted in Rs.75,000/-, the remaining amount would be Rs.60,000/-

As per the above referred Sarla Verma case, the proper multiplier Smt.Shahin W/O Amzad Patel vs The Divisionial Manager on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3247910/
8 applicable is '14'.

sentences.text: If Rs.60,000/- is multiplied by 14, it would be Rs.8,40,000/-.
Therefore, Rs.8,40,000/- is awarded under the head 'loss of dependency' as against Rs.6,98,880/- awarded by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal has committed an error in not awarding fair compensation under the head 'loss of consortium and 'loss of love and affection'.

Therefore, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance's case and Pranay Sethi's case, seven claimants are entitled to Rs.48,000/- each under the head 'loss of consortium', with 20% escalation (10% once in three years).
Accordingly, Rs.3,36,000/- (Rs.48,000 x 7)

is awarded under the head 'loss of consortium' as against Rs.1,00,000/-
towards 'loss of love and affection' and Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of estate awarded by the Tribunal.
Further, a compensation of Rs.18,000/- each is awarded under the head 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation expenses', respectively with 20% escalation.

Therefore, a sum of Rs.36,000/- (Rs.18,000 x 2) is awarded towards 'loss of estate' and 'funeral and transportation expenses'.
 12.

9 compensation as under:-

 Total Rs.12,12,000/-
 Less: Compensation awarded by the Rs.11,24,000/-
 Tribunal  Enhanced compensation Rs.88,000/-
 13.

However, in the decision rendered by this Court in MFA No.5896/2018 c/w MFA Nos.4444 in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others vs.
Venkateshan V and others, wherein a similar question arose with regard to awarding of interest, keeping in view Section 34  - 11 -  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7938  MFA No. 103487 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 102302 of 2017 of the Code of Civil Procedure, it has been held that rate of interest shall not exceed 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
